metadata.title: Enriched EBIOS RM — Business information system
metadata.description: Enriched variant of the EBIOS RM example: the baseline (workshop 1) and the ecosystem are modelled as reusable OBJECTS — business values (with AICP needs), supporting assets (linked to the business values they support), feared events (targeting a business value), ecosystem stakeholders and risk sources. Risk scenarios and measures reference these objects (business values impacted, events, sources, stakeholders, protected supporting assets). Demonstration analysis, illustrative and fictitious, generated by AI (Claude Opus 4.8).
metadata.author: C. Martin
metadata.scope: Business IS — critical digital services (business, hosting, workstations, partner interconnections)
metadata.methodology_reference: Inspired by EBIOS RM (ANSSI) and ISO 27005

levels.label: Minimal
levels.description: Vraisemblance minime : le scénario paraît difficilement réalisable ; la source de risque est peu susceptible d'agir ou le mode opératoire est très difficile à mettre en œuvre.

levels.label: Significant
levels.description: Vraisemblance significative : le scénario paraît possible ; la source de risque peut agir et le mode opératoire reste réalisable avec un effort modéré.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Vraisemblance forte : le scénario a de bonnes chances de se produire ; la source de risque est motivée et outillée, le mode opératoire est réalisable sans difficulté majeure.

levels.label: Maximal
levels.description: Vraisemblance maximale : le scénario va très probablement se produire, voire de façon récurrente ; le mode opératoire est aisé et la source de risque déterminée.

levels.label: Minor
levels.description: Gravité mineure : aucun impact opérationnel notable ni sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens. L'organisation surmonte la situation sans difficulté.

levels.label: Significant
levels.description: Gravité significative : dégradation des performances de l'activité, sans impact sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens. L'organisation surmonte la situation malgré quelques difficultés (mode dégradé).

levels.label: Serious
levels.description: Gravité grave : forte dégradation des performances de l'activité, avec d'éventuels impacts significatifs sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens. L'organisation ne surmonte la situation qu'avec de sérieuses difficultés (mode très dégradé).

levels.label: Critical
levels.description: Gravité critique : incapacité de l'organisation à assurer tout ou partie de son activité, avec d'éventuels impacts graves sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens. La survie de l'organisation peut être menacée.

criticality_levels.label: Low
criticality_levels.description: Risque faible : acceptable en l'état au regard des critères d'acceptation du risque ; à surveiller lors des revues.

criticality_levels.label: Moderate
criticality_levels.description: Risque modéré : tolérable sous conditions ; des mesures de réduction sont à envisager selon une analyse coût/bénéfice.

criticality_levels.label: High
criticality_levels.description: Risque élevé : doit être traité ; des mesures de sécurité sont planifiées et suivies pour le ramener à un niveau acceptable.

criticality_levels.label: Critical
criticality_levels.description: Risque critique : inacceptable au regard des critères d'acceptation du risque ; traitement prioritaire et immédiat requis.

risks.label: Customer data breach
risks.description: Scenario: an attacker exploits a stolen privileged account or an application vulnerability to exfiltrate the customer database. Attack path: phishing → lateral movement → database access → exfiltration. Feared event: massive disclosure of personal data.
risks.comment: Most sensitive asset of the IS (GDPR). Enhanced monitoring of privileged access and exfiltrated volumes.

custom.justification: Assessed in workshop 4: modus operandi feasible on a high-value target.
After implementing the security baseline and monitoring (SOC).

risks.label: Main server failure
risks.description: Hardware or software failure of the server hosting critical services, causing prolonged downtime. Feared event: interruption of business services.
risks.comment: Historical single point of failure, being hardened through redundancy and a DRP.

risks.label: Loss of a key skill
risks.description: Unanticipated departure of an expert holding critical, poorly documented knowledge (administration of a business application). Feared event: loss of control and continuity.
risks.comment: Dependence on a single person (bus factor = 1); documentation and pairing under way.

risks.label: GDPR non-compliance
risks.description: Non-compliant processing of personal data (legal basis, retention periods, incomplete records, processor oversight). Feared event: sanction from the supervisory authority and loss of trust.
risks.comment: Tracked by the DPO; a compliance plan is under way.

risks.label: Critical supplier delay
risks.description: Failure or delay of a critical supplier (hardware, software, managed service) affecting availability or lead times. Feared event: supply chain disruption.
risks.comment: Strong dependence on a single supplier for some components; dual sourcing initiated.

risks.label: Contractual dispute
risks.description: Contractual dispute with a client or partner (SLA interpretation, allocation of responsibilities). Feared event: litigation and legal costs. Risk assessed as tolerable.
risks.comment: Accepted residual risk (tolerable): no dedicated mitigation, annual review. Illustration of a tolerated/accepted risk.

risks.label: Site fire
risks.description: Physical incident (fire) affecting the site hosting equipment. Feared event: destruction of assets and prolonged downtime.
risks.comment: Detection/suppression in place; residual risk transferred via an insurance policy.

risks.label: Ransomware attack
risks.description: Malicious encryption of the IS by ransomware, often preceded by exfiltration (double extortion). Path: initial access (phishing / exposed VPN) → privilege escalation → propagation → encryption. Feared event: IS shutdown and ransom demand.
risks.comment: Priority scenario. Defense in depth: offline backups, EDR, SOC.

risks.label: Compromise via a third party
risks.description: Pivot attack via a third party or a third-party component (trojanized update, poorly controlled partner access). EBIOS RM strategic scenario: a stakeholder becomes an attack path. Feared event: intrusion into the IS via a trusted third party.
risks.comment: Strengthening the supplier security assurance plan and third-party audits.

risks.label: Targeted espionage / exfiltration
risks.description: Persistent espionage campaign (APT) targeting strategic information, run by a structured and well-resourced source. Feared event: stealthy, long-term exfiltration of sensitive data.
risks.comment: Advanced threat: SOC detection and network segmentation are priorities.

risks.label: Denial of service (DDoS)
risks.description: Volumetric or application-layer saturation of Internet-facing services. Hacktivist or cybercriminal source (extortion). Feared event: unavailability of online services.
risks.comment: Internet-facing services; anti-DDoS protection and CDN in place.

risks.label: Cloud misconfiguration
risks.description: Misconfiguration of a cloud service (storage made public, excessive permissions) exposing data. Source: human error or lack of review. Feared event: accidental data exposure.
risks.comment: Strengthening Infrastructure as Code and configuration review (CSPM).

measures.label: Encryption + access control + DLP
measures.description: Encryption of data at rest and in transit, privileged access management (least privilege, MFA) and data loss prevention (DLP).
measures.comment: Baseline in place; annual review of privileged accounts.

measures.label: Redundancy + disaster recovery plan (DRP)
measures.description: Redundancy of critical components and a tested disaster recovery plan (failover, defined RTO/RPO).
measures.comment: Failover being hardened; next DRP test in Q3.

measures.label: Documentation + pairing
measures.description: Formalization of administration procedures and pairing to reduce dependence on key people.

measures.label: Audit + records of processing + DPO
measures.description: Maintenance of the records of processing, appointment of a DPO, regular GDPR compliance audits and processor oversight.

measures.label: Dual sourcing + buffer stock
measures.description: Diversification of critical suppliers and a buffer stock to absorb supply disruptions.

measures.label: Detection + suppression + insurance
measures.description: Fire detection, automatic suppression and transfer of the residual risk via an insurance policy.
measures.comment: Physical controls and insurance policy up to date.

measures.label: Offline backups + EDR + training
measures.description: Immutable / offline backups (3-2-1 rule), EDR on endpoints and servers, phishing awareness training.
measures.comment: EDR deployed at 80%; quarterly awareness campaign.

measures.label: Supplier security assurance plan + third-party audits
measures.description: Contractual security requirements (security assurance plan), third-party assessment and audit, control of partner access.

measures.label: Network segmentation + 24/7 SOC
measures.description: Network partitioning (segmentation, filtering) and continuous security monitoring (SOC / SIEM) with anomaly detection.
measures.comment: Outsourced SOC in place; segmentation being extended.

measures.label: Anti-DDoS protection + CDN
measures.description: Volumetric anti-DDoS protection and CDN delivery to absorb spikes and filter malicious traffic.
measures.comment: Service in place; regular load tests.

measures.label: IaC + configuration review + CSPM
measures.description: Infrastructure as Code, configuration reviews and a cloud posture tool (CSPM) to prevent accidental exposure.
measures.comment: CSPM PoC planned; IaC industrialization scheduled.

treatments.comment: Encryption, least privilege and DLP reduce the likelihood and extent of a breach.
GDPR compliance and minimization limit the exposure of personal data.
The SOC detects abnormal access and exfiltration attempts.
Redundancy and the DRP reduce downtime duration.
Documentation and pairing reduce dependence on key people.
Records, DPO and audits ensure compliance and reduce the risk of sanction.
Encryption contributes to protecting personal data.
Dual sourcing and buffer stock absorb supply disruptions.
Third-party audits and the security assurance plan reduce the likelihood of supplier failure.
Detection and suppression limit damage; insurance transfers the residual risk.
Offline backups, EDR and training limit impact and propagation.
The SOC detects the intrusion and speeds up the response.
Access control hinders privilege escalation and propagation.
The security assurance plan and third-party audits reduce the risk of compromise via a third party.
The SOC monitors partner access and detects pivots.
Segmentation and SOC detect and slow down targeted exfiltration.
Encryption and access control limit the value of exfiltrated data.
Anti-DDoS protection absorbs saturation and keeps the service available.
The SOC detects the attack and coordinates the response.
IaC and CSPM prevent and detect configuration errors.
Audits verify configuration compliance.

description.en: ANSSI's EBIOS Risk Manager method to assess and treat digital risks through strategic and operational scenarios
International standard for information security risk management, complementary to ISO 27001
European regulation governing the processing of personal data and the associated protection obligations
European directive strengthening the cybersecurity of essential and important entities and their risk management obligations
Information system security policy defining the organisation's security rules and objectives
Direct or indirect financial losses: fraud, business interruption, penalties or remediation costs
Legal and regulatory consequences, notably GDPR penalties, litigation or contractual breaches
Damage to the image and trust of clients, partners and the public towards the organisation
Disruption of business activities and processes: unavailability, service degradation or production loss
Harm to the safety or integrity of individuals, including risks to health and physical safety
Compromise of personal data: disclosure, alteration or loss affecting the data subjects

description.fr: Justification de la cotation : choix de la vraisemblance et de la gravité.
description.en: Rationale for the assessment: choice of likelihood and severity.
description.it: Motivazione della valutazione: scelta di verosimiglianza e gravità.

description.en: Understand context, assets and risks to govern cybersecurity (NIST CSF Identify function)
Implement safeguards to limit the impact of an incident (NIST CSF Protect function)
Promptly identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event (NIST CSF Detect function)
Act on a detected incident to contain and reduce its effects (NIST CSF Respond function)
Restore capabilities and services impaired by an incident (NIST CSF Recover function)
Control based on technological means: encryption, segmentation, logging or access control
Control relating to governance and procedures: policies, awareness, management of roles and responsibilities
Physical security control protecting premises, equipment and media against access and incidents
Control of a contractual or regulatory nature: clauses, compliance commitments and subcontracting obligations
Control reducing the likelihood of a risk scenario occurring
Control limiting the severity of consequences should the risk scenario occur
Control enabling detection of the risk scenario's occurrence in order to react
Control transferring all or part of the risk to a third party, through insurance or outsourcing

custom.socle_securite: ANSSI IT hygiene guide and internal security policy (ISSP); GDPR compliance for the personal data processed by the business IS.
custom.recevabilite: Admissible study: scope of the business IS framed, business values and supporting assets identified, ecosystem and risk sources assessed; security baseline evaluated (see requirements).

values.nom: Massive disclosure of the customer database
values.impacts: GDPR fine, reputational harm, loss of customer trust.

values.nom: Prolonged unavailability of the business software
values.impacts: Production halt, financial losses, delivery delays.
Invasion of employees' privacy, GDPR fine.

values.motivation: Financial gain through extortion (encryption and threat of disclosure).
values.objectif_vise: Encrypt the IS and demand a ransom.
values.justification: Primary threat: ransomware very active against SMEs/mid-caps.
Retained given the value of the data and possible long-term positioning.

values.description: Employee or provider with internal access.

values.justification: Dismissed: interest and capability judged low in this context.
Dismissed: limited impact (temporary unavailability) and low targeting.
values.description: Activist collective carrying out denial-of-service actions.

values.chemin: Phishing → execution → propagation → encryption of servers and online backups.
values.ecosysteme: Cloud host and outsourcer provide access and administration.
values.mesures_ecosysteme: Require immutable backups and partitioning of administration access.

values.chemin: Compromise of a privileged access → database extraction → threat of disclosure.
values.ecosysteme: ERP vendor with remote maintenance access.
values.mesures_ecosysteme: Control the vendor's remote access (bastion, MFA, logging).

values.nom: Compromise via the supply chain (ERP vendor)
values.chemin: Compromise of the vendor → trojanized update → alteration of billing data.
values.ecosysteme: Vendor and outsourcer in the update chain.
values.mesures_ecosysteme: Verify update integrity; contractual security clauses.

values.nom: HR data leak via the payroll processor
values.chemin: Access misuse at the processor → extraction of payroll data.
values.ecosysteme: Payroll processor receiving the HR data.
values.mesures_ecosysteme: Audit of the processor; minimization of the data transmitted.

values.nom: Denial of service on customer relations
values.chemin: DDoS campaign → saturation of exposed services → unavailability.
values.ecosysteme: Cloud host on the front line.
values.mesures_ecosysteme: Anti-DDoS protection and continuity plan on the host side.

values.chemin: Targeted phishing, loader execution, privilege escalation, lateral movement, backup disabling, encryption.
values.mitre: TA0001 Initial Access (Phishing T1566) → TA0002 Execution → TA0004 Privilege Escalation → TA0008 Lateral Movement → TA0040 Impact (Inhibit System Recovery T1490 + Data Encrypted for Impact T1486)

values.chemin: Theft of admin credentials, database access, encrypted extraction, exfiltration.
values.mitre: TA0006 Credential Access → TA0007 Discovery → TA0009 Collection (Archive Collected Data T1560) → TA0010 Exfiltration

values.chemin: Vendor compromise, injection into a patch, deployment, data alteration.
values.mitre: TA0001 Initial Access (Supply Chain Compromise T1195) → TA0002 Execution → TA0040 Impact (Data Manipulation T1565)

values.chemin: Use of a processor account, extraction of payslips, external transmission.
values.mitre: TA0001 Initial Access (Trusted Relationship T1199) → TA0009 Collection → TA0010 Exfiltration
values.maillon_limitant: Logging and partitioning at the processor

values.chemin: Botnet, saturation of bandwidth and exposed application services.
values.mitre: TA0040 Impact (Network Denial of Service T1498)

values.reference: ANSSI hygiene guide — measure 37: Define and apply a backup policy for critical components
values.remediation: Set up immutable/offline backups and test restorations.

values.exigence: MFA on privileged and remote access
values.reference: ANSSI hygiene guide — measure 13: Favour strong authentication wherever possible
values.ecart: MFA missing on some administration access.
values.remediation: Generalize MFA and use an administration bastion.

values.reference: ANSSI hygiene guide — measure 19: Segment the network and set up partitioning between these zones
ANSSI hygiene guide — measure 36: Enable and configure logs on the most important components
values.remediation: Deploy centralized collection and detection rules.

values.reference: ANSSI hygiene guide — measure 34: Define an update policy for information system components
values.ecart: Patching delays too long on the ERP.
values.remediation: Formalize a patch cycle and tracking of critical vulnerabilities.
